messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm drafting an RFP-style ask for policy-slices prioritization + fallback playbook. Need input by EOD Wed. TL;DR: define launch gates, per-slice SLAs, fallback sequence, and rough cost impact.

ajay: Can you call out candidate SLA bands? p50/p95/p99 targets per slice would help. Also want to know if we treat model variants as first-class fallbacks or only region failovers.

jordan: Suggest three tenant classes: enterprise (gold), standard (silver), best-effort (bronze). Each has different isolation + routing expectations. Enterprise => dedicated pools + cross-region affinity; bronze => shared pools with aggressive batching.

sasha: +1 on the classes. Proposed launch gate checklist: perf tests (latency & tail), cost model validated, canary rollout plan (1% -> 10% -> 100%), ops playbook & runbook rehearsed.

maria: here's a tiny policy template I'm prototyping — want feedback on fields we must require vs optional:
```
policy:
  slice: enterprise
  sla:
    p50_ms: 25
    p95_ms: 60
    p99_ms: 120
  fallback_sequence:
    - region: same, model_variant: same
    - region: region-b, model_variant: same
    - region: region-b, model_variant: quantized-smaller
  isolation: dedicated-pool
  cost_impact_estimate: high
```

ajay: That looks good. A couple notes: add `cold-start_tolerance` and `kv-cache_affinity` fields. Also flag whether prefix caching is tenant-scoped (true for enterprise).

jordan: From infra POV, we need TTLs for cross-region affinity and an eviction hierarchy: 1) spill to paired region, 2) switch model to lower-cost quant, 3) queue requests (graceful backpressure). We should quantify expected RPS at each step.

sasha: For launch gating: require a canned chaos test that simulates a region loss and validates fallback sequence less than X seconds; require cost alerting (burn rate) and rollback trigger conditions.

maria: Customer asks we've captured: strict isolation for financials customers, sub-100ms p99 requests for embed-heavy customers, and cross-region DR for EU customers with data locality needs. We're balancing those vs ops cost.

ops-bot: doc uploaded: https://redwood.docs/slices/rfp-draft (uploaded by maria) :pushpin:

ajay: My prioritization suggestion (1-line matrix): impact-to-customer x implementation-effort. Enterprise isolation + cross-region DR = highest impact but high effort. Quick wins: routing templates + fallback policy framework (low effort, unlocks many cases).

maria: Agree. Action items: ajay to propose exact SLA numbers for each slice by Tue morning; jordan to draft eviction hierarchy + estimated infra delta; sasha to author gating checklist + rehearsal plan. I'll synthesize into RFP and circulate. Thanks! :thumbsup:

jordan: one more thing — can we standardize naming for fallback models (regionB-quant-v1) so runbooks are unambiguous? small naming doc would reduce on-call confusion.

maria: yes — added to my to-do list. Will include a naming appendix in the RFP.

sasha: Rehearsal suggestion: include an oncall-runbook tabletop with simulated billing spike + region failover. 30m session per squad.

maria: awesome. closing loop here — will share updated draft tomorrow morning and schedule a 30m sync.
